rationale: Review 2026-11-12T21:11:56Z to 2026-11-12T21:16:36Z UTC. All cited text files re-hashed with one script against their recorded text_sha256 and every source_fingerprints entry; all matched. cruden.py number search (snapshot 28504e0c..., 49,073 readable sources) run for the order. Identity: held FR text (11 FR 6957, jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_9739.txt) prints EXECUTIVE ORDER 9739, signed June 20, 1946, prescribing regulations for transportation expenses of employees transferred on the return of departmental functions to the seat of government; matches the dossier. Basis: held FR text of EO 9834 (12 FR 1883) sec. 3 reads 'Executive Order No. 9739 of June 20, 1946, is hereby revoked, except that it shall continue to be applicable, so long as necessary, with respect to the payment of expenses incident to any return of departmental functions to the seat of government ordered prior to November 1, 1946, and incomplete on that date'; sec. 4 makes EO 9834 effective as of November 1, 1946. The revocation reaches the whole order (all three sections); the only survival is the express saving. Savings: the saved application is confined to expense payments for a closed class of returns ordered before November 1, 1946 and still incomplete then, and lasts only 'so long as necessary'; it has no possible operative object on 2026-10-14, so the order is not in force at the cutoff, while (as the decision itself says) the date the saving was exhausted is not shown and the lifecycle end date stays open. Earlier end/partial scope: cruden found only the order itself and EO 9834 (FR and APP texts); no earlier revocation or revival. History observations (OFR catalog, 1989 codification) carry no flags. Accept.
